html:
The Kingdom of Croatia was the medieval state of the Croats on the Adriatic coast and inland, ruled by native kings from about 925, when Tomislav is first called king, until 1102.

The Croats had settled the area in the 600s and became Christian, keeping close ties to Rome. Under Tomislav, Croatia held off the Magyars and Bulgarians. Later kings such as Peter Krešimir IV ruled the Dalmatian coast towns. Croatian priests used the Glagolitic script, as on the Baška tablet, in their liturgy. When the last king, Petar Snačić, died fighting in 1097, the crown passed by the Pacta conventa to the kings of Hungary. Croatian statehood today traces itself to this kingdom.
